content:
The test image shows the inside of a corn husk peeled back, revealing:
- **Orange-brown fibrous husk tissue** with **numerous small black dots (pycnidia)** scattered uniformly across the surface
- **Brown/tan discolored kernels** at the top
- The overall dried, mummified appearance of the ear

The numerous small black pycnidia embedded in the husk tissue are the diagnostic hallmark of **Diplodia ear rot**. The symptom description explicitly states: *"Raised black bumps (pycnidia) develop on moldy husks or kernels late in the season."* The white mold phase appears to have progressed to a later dried stage here.

The reference images confirm bleached husks and grayish-brown kernel discoloration — consistent with what's visible.

This matches the diagnostic description of raised black bumps (pycnidia) on moldy husks, and is distinct from other ear rots which lack pycnidia (Gibberella/Fusarium show pink/white mold; Aspergillus shows olive-green powdery mold)."}
